question: Which host filesystem policy contract should OpenClaw support here, and how should shell-mediated `exec` access be represented in that contract?
rationale: This defines an operator-facing security boundary and public config surface, with competing open designs and compatibility risk that automation cannot choose safely.

options.title: Choose a versioned `tools.fs` policy
options.body: Define the accepted allow/deny or roots contract, require normalization/deny-precedence semantics, and explicitly document whether exec is covered now or split to a linked follow-up.

options.title: Land file-tools first, split exec
options.body: Accept a narrower filesystem-tools implementation while keeping shell-mediated access tracked separately so operators are not promised full sandboxing.

options.title: Reject core config expansion
options.body: Keep the current `workspaceOnly`/Docker/OS-user model and direct operators to external hardening, accepting that this issue remains unsupported in core.

recommendation.title: Choose a versioned `tools.fs` policy
recommendation.body: Define the accepted allow/deny or roots contract, require normalization/deny-precedence semantics, and explicitly document whether exec is covered now or split to a linked follow-up.

likelyOwner.reason: He is tied to the current workspaceOnly policy history and prior maintainer-side review of this exact issue, so he is the best available owner for the policy decision.
